# Twenty-seven

{~~He went down to the cellar and looked at the barrels.~>He went down to
the cellar the way a man goes down to look at a debt.

The barrels stood in two rows along the north wall, thirty-one of them,
each one stencilled with a year and a row number in his father's square
hand. The stencils had been made from a set of brass letters that lived
in a cigar box on the shelf above the press, and the brass letters had
been bought in Genoa in 1897 by a man who had never seen a grape grown
west of the Apennines.

He put his hand flat on the head of the nearest barrel. It was cold, and
under the cold there was the faint give of wood that has been wet on the
inside for thirty years.

Nothing in the cellar was worth anything now. That was the arithmetic and
he had done the arithmetic every night for a month. What he had not done,
until this particular night with the lamp guttering and the fog coming
in under the door, was stand in front of it and let it be true.~~}

He was still standing there when the lamp went out.
